## What

The self-improvement watchdog classifies each failed `tool_invocations` row into
`structural | transient | caller | rate-limit`. That ONE logical rule had TWO
implementations:

- `classifyToolError(...)` — a TS fn (the "documented source of truth"), and
- a hand-typed SQL `CASE … END` inside `collectToolErrorSignals` (what actually
  runs in-DB at scale).

They were "kept in sync" by a comment — and had **silently drifted**. A
`handler_error` row whose message starts `invalid_args: …` classified `caller`
in SQL (`LIKE 'invalid_args:%'`) but `structural` in TS (its `error_code` branch
never checked the message prefix). 100+ high-volume rows/day disagreed — the SQL
filed them correctly as caller-DX, the "source of truth" fn said structural. Two
of the three prior watchdog classifier bugs were the same shape: a fix landed in
one impl, the other lagged.

## Why it's the trap

Dual implementations of one rule never stay in sync under maintenance. A comment
("keep in sync with the SQL CASE") is not a mechanism — it's a hope. Nothing
fails when they diverge; the divergence just quietly mis-routes work.

## The fix (watchdog-and-exposed-systems-improvement-2026-06-18 P-011)

Make an **ordered rule table the single source** and GENERATE both impls from it:

```ts
// tool-error-classifier.ts
export const TOOL_ERROR_RULES = [ /* {class, errorCodes?, statuses?, messagePattern?} */ ];
export function classifyToolError(...) { /* walks the table */ }
export function toolErrorClassSqlCase(sql) { /* GENERATES `CASE WHEN … THEN … END` from the table */ }
```

`collectToolErrorSignals` embeds `${toolErrorClassSqlCase(sql)} AS class`. Now the
TS fn and the SQL CASE cannot drift — they're the same table.

Two constraints that make this work:

1. **Dual-engine patterns.** Each `messagePattern` is a string that must be a
   valid regex in BOTH Postgres `~*` (POSIX ERE) AND JS `new RegExp(p, 'i')`. Use
   only constructs that mean the same in both (`|`, `?`, `*`, `+`, `^`, `(…)`,
   `[ _-]`, literals). NO JS-only `\s`/`\d`/`\b`/lookarounds and NO POSIX
   `[[:alpha:]]` — those are exactly how the two engines would disagree. A
   module-load + unit guard rejects a pattern that won't compile as a JS RegExp.
2. **A real-PG parity test with teeth.** `tool-error-classifier.integration.test.ts`
   loads a committed real-corpus fixture (high-volume distinct shapes sampled from
   `tool_invocations`), runs the GENERATED SQL `CASE` (real `~*`) over it, and
   asserts row-by-row agreement with the TS fn. If `~*` and JS `RegExp` ever
   diverge on a real shape, it goes red. The pure unit test pins each bucket to
   its correct class so the next misclassification is caught before it floods a
   lane.

## When you'll need this

Any time one logical decision has two homes — a TS predicate + a SQL `CASE`/`WHERE`,
a client check + a server check, a regex used in code + in a migration. Don't
mirror by hand; lift the rule to data and generate (or share) both, then add a
parity test that runs the REAL second impl. The same module also generalized the
dedup fingerprint to more classes (P-012) by reading one shared
`FINGERPRINTED_TOOL_ERROR_CLASSES` set from both the SQL and the TS key builder —
same principle.
